content: 1. The metabolism of oglitazone is influenced by hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Exercise caution and monitor closely when co-administered. 2. Clarithromycin reduces the effects of piperacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. 3. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 4. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of pitavastatin through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may elevate the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor. 5. Clarithromycin elevates the levels or effects of polatuzumab vedotin by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase unconjugated MMAE exposure, leading to heightened toxicities. Use caution and monitor. 6. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of posaconazole by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 7. Clarithromycin raises pravastatin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for myopathy and do not exceed a pravastatin dose of 40 mg/day when co-administered. OATP1B1 inhibitors may further increase the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor. 8. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of praziquantel by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 9. Clarithromycin elevates prednisolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. This may lead to toxic steroid concentrations and altered mental status. Use caution and monitor. 10. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of propafenone by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 11. Clarithromycin reduces pyridoxine levels by altering intestinal flora, applicable only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 12. Clarithromycin increases quazepam levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 13. Clarithromycin and quetiapine both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of toxicity. Avoid use with other QT-prolonging drugs and in patients with risk factors for QT prolongation. Monitor closely with ECG. 14. Clarithromycin raises quinine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 15. Clarithromycin increases quizartinib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Interrupt quizartinib during strong CYP3A4 inhibitor use. Monitor ECG frequently if co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. 16. Clarithromycin elevates rabeprazole levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 17. Clarithromycin and ranolazine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 18. Rifabutin reduces clarithromycin levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 19. Rifampin decreases clarithromycin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 20. Clarithromycin increases rifaximin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 21. Clarithromycin raises rilpivirine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Rilpivirine increases clarithromycin toxicity via QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor. Avoid co-administration with drugs that increase the risk of Torsades de Pointes. 22. Clarithromycin elevates riociguat levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 23. Clarithromycin increases ripretinib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increases systemic exposure to ripretinib and its active metabolite (DP-5439), heightening the risk of adverse reactions. Use caution and monitor. 24. Clarithromycin raises risperidone levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 25. Clarithromycin increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 26. Clarithromycin elevates roflumilast levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 27. Clarithromycin increases romidepsin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 28. Clarithromycin raises rosiglitazone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially causing hypoglycemia. Monitor glucose levels closely. 29. Rucaparib increases clarithromycin levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Adjust CYP3A4 substrate dosages if clinically indicated. 30. Clarithromycin elevates sacubitril/valsartan levels through OATP1B1 inhibition, increasing valsartan systemic exposure. Use caution and monitor. 31. Clarithromycin raises salmeterol levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 32. Clarithromycin increases saxagliptin levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 33. Clarithromycin elevates seladelpar levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution in poor CYP2C9 metabolizers co-administered with moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. 34. Selpercatinib increases clarithromycin toxicity via QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor. 35. Clarithromycin raises silodosin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 36. Clarithromycin increases sirolimus levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 37. Clarithromycin reduces the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering colonic bacterial flora needed for drug activation. Use caution and monitor. 38. Clarithromycin elevates sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 39. Sorafenib and clarithromycin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 40. St. John’s Wort reduces clarithromycin levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 41. Stiripentol affects clarithromycin metabolism via CYP3A4 inhibition and induction. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Adjust CYP3A4 substrate dosages as needed. 42. Clarithromycin increases streptomycin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 43. Clarithromycin raises sufentanil levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentrations, leading to prolonged adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. Use caution and monitor. 44. Clarithromycin and sulfamethoxazole both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 45. Clarithromycin elevates tacrolimus levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 46. Clarithromycin increases tamoxifen levels by reducing its metabolism to N-desmethyl tamoxifen, an active metabolite. Use caution and monitor. 47. Clarithromycin raises tasimelteon levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 48. Tazemetostat reduces clarithromycin levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 49. Tecovirimat decreases clarithromycin levels by weakly inducing CYP3A4. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if co-administered. 50. Clarithromycin and telavancin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 51. Clarithromycin increases teniposide levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 52. Clarithromycin raises terbinafine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 53. Clarithromycin elevates tezacaftor levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Adjust tezacaftor dosage regimen if co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 54. Clarithromycin reduces thiamine levels by altering intestinal flora, applicable only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor. 55. Clarithromycin increases ticagrelor levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid use with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Use caution and monitor. 56. Clarithromycin raises tinidazole levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 57. Clarithromycin elevates tisotumab vedotin levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. MMAE, its active metabolite, is a CYP3A4 substrate. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to unconjugated MMAE, heightening the risk of adverse effects. Use caution and monitor. 58. Clarithromycin increases tobramycin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 59. Clarithromycin raises tolvaptan levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor. 60. Clarithromycin elevates tramadol levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 61. Clarithromycin and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 62. Clarithromycin increases trimipramine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 63. Triptorelin increases clarithromycin toxicity via QTc prolongation, raising the risk of Torsades de Pointes. Use caution and monitor. 64. Clarithromycin and tropisetron both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 65. Clarithromycin raises ulipristal levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 66. Clarithromycin increases umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Vilanterol is a CYP3A4 substrate, and co-administration with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 67. Clarithromycin elevates upadacitinib levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor, especially with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 68. Clarithromycin raises valbenazine levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. 69. Clarithromycin increases valsartan levels through OATP1B1 inhibition, increasing systemic exposure. Use caution and monitor. 70. Clarithromycin elevates vamorolone levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce vamorolone starting dose to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day for patients weighing over 50 kg. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 71. Clarithromycin raises vardenafil levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 72. Clarithromycin increases velpatasvir levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 73. Clarithromycin and venlafaxine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 74. Clarithromycin elevates verapamil levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor.
